frameworks.name: Continuous Action Model
frameworks.definition: Consistent work across time horizon creates readiness for all opportunities; timing becomes irrelevant when preparation is continuous.

frameworks.name: Skill-Opportunity Multiplication Loop
frameworks.definition: Each skill acquired expands the set of executable opportunities; broader skill portfolio opens exponentially more paths.

claims.text: Perfect timing is a myth, but perfect preparation is attainable. On a long enough time horizon, continuous work ensures you will be ready when opportunities arrive (Alex Hormozi, MoreMozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: continuous work creates readiness and preparation; readiness intersects with opportunities regardless of when they arrive
bounded_by: Does not apply to time-bounded markets with fixed windows
Does not guarantee specific opportunity timing

claims.text: The likelihood of being present at three specific opportunity moments is very low if you attempt to time your work and rest cycles; but if you work continuously, you will be ready whenever opportunities arise.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: choice between sporadic work and continuous work
claims.mechanism: continuous preparation eliminates timing dependency; sporadic work creates misalignment between readiness and opportunity occurrence

claims.text: Starting is the perfect condition. It creates the conditions for opportunity to be capitalized on (Alex Hormozi).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: action initiates feedback loops that reveal capability; feedback loops generate learning and opportunity visibility
bounded_by: Does not imply that starting without resources or skill is optimal

claims.text: The more you do, the more you see you can do. Opportunities multiply with skill acquisition. The better you get at doing stuff, the more things you know you would be able to do and win at (Alex Hormozi, from firsthand experience).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: each skill unlocks perception of new opportunities; cumulative skills expand the set of solvable problems exponentially

claims.text: The goal is to gain as many skills as possible so that you have access to the maximum number of potential opportunities.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: broader skill portfolio increases the probability of holding relevant capabilities when new opportunities arise
bounded_by: Does not apply to narrow specialization requirements (e.g., deep surgical expertise)

claims.text: People wait for the right moment, but when you have unlimited skills, the world of opportunities opens to you. Elon Musk could build a city in the middle of the ocean because he has the skills; he spent all of his younger years developing different skills and becoming a polymath (Alex Hormozi, example of Elon Musk).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: demonstrated capability across multiple domains creates option value and buyer confidence for ambitious projects
bounded_by: Does not apply to early-career founders with single-domain expertise

claims.text: If you get good, you will never have a shortage of opportunities.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: definition of 'good' as mastery in relevant domain(s)
claims.mechanism: demonstrated excellence creates demand from others seeking to acquire or partner with that excellence
bounded_by: Assumes markets exist for the developed skill

claims.text: There is a 10-stage roadmap from zero to $100M+ revenue that less than 1% of companies complete. At each stage defined by headcount growth, there are distinct constraints across eight business functions, with identifiable symptoms of constraint and specific graduation steps (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com portfolio, tested across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: multiple business model types tested: software, physical products, services, brick-and-mortar
claims.mechanism: each revenue stage imposes structural constraints that prevent growth until resolved; constraints differ by business function and stage
bounded_by: Tested across multiple model types but universal applicability to all business types not claimed

examples.text: Elon Musk spent his younger years developing diverse skills and becoming a polymath, which opens to him a world of opportunities such as building a city in the middle of the ocean. Because he possesses the skills across multiple domains, he has option value that others do not.

practices.text: Work continuously across your lifetime rather than attempting to time work and rest cycles around expected opportunities.
Start immediately rather than waiting for perfect conditions; action creates the conditions for opportunity capitalization.
Accumulate skills across diverse domains to expand the number of opportunities you can execute on.
Use the Acquisition.com 10-stage roadmap to diagnose your current constraint and graduation requirements across eight business functions.
